column1: # Requirements for Mica::Deflate, Mica::Zlib and Mica::Gzip (milestone Z1, the
# pure-Crystal Inflate decoder): the decoder requirements of RFC 1951
# (DEFLATE), RFC 1950 (zlib) and RFC 1952 (gzip), the public API, and the
# decode limits. Where zlib 1.2.12 and the letter of an RFC differ, Mica
# follows zlib and the summary says so.
# The DEFLATE-LIMIT-* ids are shared: spec/deflate/bomb_spec.cr and
# spec/deflate/differential_spec.cr (the fuzz work) cover them as well, and
# the ids those specs add are merged into this catalog.

column3: Data elements are read from the least significant bit of each byte; Huffman codes are read most significant bit first and extra bits least significant bit first
Codes are rebuilt from code lengths alone: shorter codes first, and codes of one length in symbol order
Literal/length and distance codes of every length from 1 to 15 bits decode
A set of code lengths that claims more codes than exist (oversubscribed) is rejected for all three alphabets
An incomplete literal/length or distance code is rejected, except the zlib case of exactly one code of length 1 (Mica follows zlib 1.2.12 here; the RFC only allows it for the distance code)
Data that uses the unassigned code of an accepted incomplete code is rejected
Each block starts with BFINAL (1 bit) and BTYPE (2 bits) at any bit position
BTYPE 11 is rejected
A stream is any sequence of stored, fixed and dynamic blocks, and their output is concatenated
Decoding ends with the block that sets BFINAL; a stream whose last block does not set it is truncated
The bits between a stored block header and the next byte boundary are ignored, whatever their value
NLEN must be the one's complement of LEN; any other value is rejected
LEN bytes are copied to the output, for every LEN from 0 to 65,535
Symbols 0 to 255 are literal bytes
Symbol 256 ends the block
Length symbols 257 to 285 and their extra bits give lengths 3 to 258
Length symbol 284 with extra bits 31 decodes as length 258 (Mica follows zlib 1.2.12 and libdeflate; the RFC assigns 258 to symbol 285 only)
Distance symbols 0 to 29 and their extra bits give distances 1 to 32,768
Literal/length symbols 286 and 287 and distance symbols 30 and 31 are rejected when they occur in the data
A back reference may overlap the bytes it produces (length greater than distance)
A back reference may reach into the output of earlier blocks of any type
A back reference may reach exactly 32,768 bytes back, also after the output has passed 32,768 bytes
A back reference to before the first output byte is rejected
BTYPE 01 uses the fixed literal/length code (8, 9, 7 and 8 bits) and 5-bit distance codes
HLIT declares 257 to 286 literal/length code lengths; 287 and 288 are rejected
HDIST declares 1 to 30 distance code lengths; 31 and 32 are rejected
HCLEN declares 4 to 19 code length code lengths, sent in the order 16 17 18 0 8 7 9 6 10 5 11 4 12 3 13 2 14 1 15; the ones not sent are zero
The code length code must be complete: an incomplete one is rejected even with a single code (zlib 1.2.12)
Code length symbols 0 to 15 are literal code lengths
Symbol 16 repeats the previous code length 3 to 6 times, and is rejected when no code length precedes it
Symbol 17 repeats a zero length 3 to 10 times
Symbol 18 repeats a zero length 11 to 138 times
The literal/length and distance code lengths form one sequence, so a repeat may run from the first alphabet into the second
A repeat that runs past HLIT + HDIST code lengths is rejected
A literal/length code that gives symbol 256 no code is rejected (zlib 1.2.12)
One distance code is sent as one code of length 1, with one unused code
A distance code with no codes is accepted for a block of literals only; a length symbol in such a block is rejected
CM must be 8 (deflate); any other compression method is rejected
CINFO from 0 to 7 is accepted and above 7 rejected; distances are checked against the 32 KiB window and the output so far, not against the declared window (zlib 1.2.12 without INFLATE_STRICT)
CMF * 256 + FLG must be a multiple of 31
FLEVEL has no effect on decoding
With FDICT set a 4-byte DICTID follows FLG, and the stream is rejected unless the caller supplied the dictionary whose Adler-32 it is
A preset dictionary is the history before the first output byte: back references reach into its last 32,768 bytes and no further
The trailer is the Adler-32 of the uncompressed data, most significant byte first; a mismatch is a checksum error
Adler-32 is two sums modulo 65521, s1 starting at 1 and s2 at 0, returned as s2 * 65536 + s1
A gzip file is a series of members, and the output is the output of each member in order
A member starts with ID1 0x1f and ID2 0x8b
CM must be 8 (deflate)
A member with FLG bit 5, 6 or 7 set is rejected
FTEXT is reported and has no effect on the data
MTIME (4 bytes, least significant first), XFL and OS are reported, and every value is accepted
With FEXTRA set, XLEN (2 bytes, least significant first) and that many bytes follow the fixed header
With FNAME set, a zero-terminated file name follows
With FCOMMENT set, a zero-terminated comment follows
The optional fields come in the order extra field, file name, comment, header CRC, in every combination of the flags
With FHCRC set, CRC16 must equal the low 16 bits of the CRC-32 of the header bytes before it
The trailer CRC32 must equal the CRC-32 of the member's uncompressed data
The trailer ISIZE must equal the size of the member's uncompressed data modulo 2^32
CRC-32 uses the polynomial 0xEDB88320 with initial value and final XOR 0xFFFFFFFF
Deflate.decode, Zlib.decode and Gzip.decode return the whole output of a valid stream
A Reader gives the same output, or the same error at the same input offset, as the one-shot decode, however its input is chunked
A Reader read one output byte at a time, over input that arrives one byte at a time, gives the same result as the one-shot decode
A Reader is a read-only IO: it reads zero bytes at the end of the stream, refuses writes, and closes its source only with sync_close
Every decode entry point takes limits and timeout as required arguments with no default
DecodeLimits has the presets REQUEST_BODY, HTTP_CLIENT_RESPONSE, WEBSOCKET_MESSAGE and TRUSTED_ASSET, and custom starts from REQUEST_BODY
Stream errors are MalformedStreamError (a Mica::ParseError) with the input byte offset; TruncatedStreamError and ChecksumError are its subclasses
Input that ends anywhere inside a stream raises TruncatedStreamError
A whole byte after the final block (raw), after the Adler-32 (zlib), or after a member that does not start another member (gzip) is rejected; padding bits in the last byte are ignored
Gzip::Reader reports each member's header fields in list_of_headers
CRC32.update and Adler32.update continue a running checksum, so any split of the input gives the same value
Output past max_output_bytes raises DecodeLimitError naming max_output_bytes; output of exactly the limit is allowed
Once the output passes 1 MiB, output larger than max_ratio times the input consumed raises DecodeLimitError naming max_ratio
A back reference farther than max_window_bytes, or a zlib header declaring a larger window, raises DecodeLimitError naming max_window_bytes
A gzip stream with more than max_members members raises DecodeLimitError naming max_members
A gzip member whose FEXTRA, FNAME and FCOMMENT bytes together pass max_metadata_bytes raises DecodeLimitError naming max_metadata_bytes
A decode that needs more work than its limits allow raises Mica::WorkBudgetExceededError
A decode that runs past its timeout raises Mica::DeadlineExceededError
A decompression bomb allocates at most about twice max_output_bytes one-shot, and a fixed 224 KiB of buffers streaming, before its limit error
Long runs of empty stored or dynamic blocks are charged per block, so the work budget and the deadline stop them
Across generated, encoder-made and mutated streams, Mica and system zlib agree: the same output, or both reject

With stop_at_end, a Deflate or Zlib Reader takes from its source only the bytes of the stream (through peek when the source has it, one byte per read otherwise), so what follows the stream stays in the source
